reference_boundary: Appearance-only comparison of visible face shape, eye aperture and spacing, lower-face shape, hairline, and long dark hair. No identity, same-person, or sensitive-trait claim is made.

common_gates.evidence: The original adult fictional subject keeps a readable oval face, comparable eye aperture and spacing, tapered lower face, dark hairline, and long dark wavy hair from the appearance reference.
The subject reads as an adult at native and thumbnail scales, with natural facial proportions and no doll-like or childlike reshaping.
Head, torso, arm, glove, control, telescope assembly, window, and solar display form one coherent laboratory scene at both review scales.
The visible gloved hand wraps the telescope-console control with contact pressure and a plausible wrist-to-control relation.

Tiny interface numerals and pseudo-glyphs are present, but the solar disk, active region, burst, and loops carry the scientific meaning without captions, signage, or a watermark supplying any missing gate.

profile_gates.evidence: The thumbnail clearly shows the complete false-color solar disk, and the bright burst is visibly located on that disk.
One concentrated, magnetically structured active region remains identifiable around the primary bright source at both scales.
A compact, saturated white-orange brightening occupies the localized active region in the native image.
Bright curved coronal loops visibly originate at and remain connected to the burst within the same disk quadrant rather than forming a detached front.
The blue-gold analytical palette, whole-disk presentation, and color scale read as a false-color solar observation rather than a detached fictional explosion.
